subject: Draft mutual action plan: concrete success definitions, exit scenarios, and acceptance tests
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Susan Ortega <susan.ortega@curahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft MAP: success definitions & exit scenarios for CuraHealth eval

Hi Susan —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. As promised, attached is a first-pass mutual action plan that translates the evaluation goals you described into concrete success criteria, exit gates, and a short acceptance test suite. High-level items in this draft: 

- Success criteria (measurable): p95 latency < 250ms for 95% of user flows, end-to-end inference cost < $0.004/token on typical workload, semantic-accuracy concordance >= 92% on your curated prompt set, <1% unacceptable hallucination rate on the test corpus.
- Exit gates: security signoff (SOC2 evidence + enclave config), performance baseline (sustained throughput with 95% pass on latency), UX acceptance (stakeholder demo + acceptance sign-off), procurement milestone (PO or signed SOW).
- Acceptance tests: smoke generation tests, golden-prompt concordance set (50 prompts), red-team sample (20 edge cases), sustained load run (2 hours at expected TPS), integration verification (PII handling and audit log sample).

Action items for you: please confirm (a) whether the accuracy/concordance target aligns with your QA team, (b) which stakeholders need to be present for the final demo, and (c) any additional must-have security evidence beyond SOC2 and an ingestion audit log.

Proposed timeline (draft):
- Week 0: finalize MAP and procurement kickoff
- Week 1–2: test harness + integration work
- Week 3: performance & smoke validation
- Week 4: stakeholder demo + signoff

Attachment: MAP_v1_CuraHealth.xlsx — the sheet titled "Acceptance Tests" breaks the items above into owners and pass/fail criteria. I put suggested owners for Redwood and a proposed acceptance cadence.

If that looks right I can update and send a version with two decision points clearly marked (performance gate, security gate) for your legal/procurement.

Thanks — looking forward to your feedback.

— Priyom
Priyom Das | Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0147

From: Susan Ortega <susan.ortega@curahealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@curahealth.com>
Date: 2028-08-24T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: success definitions & exit scenarios for CuraHealth eval

On Wed, Aug 23, 2028 at 9:12 AM Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for taking the time yesterday...

Thanks, Priyom — this is very helpful and a good starting point. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Concordance target: our QA lead needs the concordance target to be at 94% for the clinical triage prompts (we can relax for administrative prompts). Can you separate the golden-prompt set into "clinical" and "non-clinical" buckets and show pass/fail per-bucket?
2) Security evidence: SOC2 is good; we also need an attestation on data residency (EU vs US) for records processed during the pilot and a sample of audit logs for admin actions.
3) Demo attendees: Clinical product lead (Dr. Patel), Head of QA (Lindsay), and Procurement (cc'd).

Procurement asked whether we can tie the procurement milestone to a short proof-of-performance report rather than waiting for full signoff; they prefer a PO + 30 days to reduce procurement lead time.

I'll review the attachment in detail and get back with specifics by Friday.

— Susan
Susan Ortega
Director, Product — CuraHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-24T14:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: success definitions & exit scenarios for CuraHealth eval

Priyom / Ben — quick internal note after reading Susan's points. I updated the acceptance tests and exit gates as follows (I'm attaching a short markdown runbook):

- Split golden-set into clinical (50 prompts) / administrative (50 prompts); target: clinical concordance >= 94%, administrative concordance >= 90%.
- Add data-residency attestation step under Security Gate; add evidence owner = Security & Compliance (Redwood) and requested artifact = sample audit logs (7 days).
- Procurement path: we can support PO + 30d provisional staging. Add a decision point in the MAP: "PO-staged -> allow limited capacity access for 30d".

Runbook highlights:
- If performance run fails (p95 > 300ms), automatic rollback to smaller model variant and notify both teams; re-run with adjusted batch size within 48 hours.
- If clinical concordance falls 2 points below threshold during smoke tests, freeze demo and open an urgent evaluation ticket with ML Ops.

I'll publish MAP_v1.1 with the split golden-set and the new procurement clause. Ben — can you draft a one-paragraph note for procurement explaining the PO + 30d staging (they'll want liability language)?

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Susan Ortega <susan.ortega@curahealth.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-25T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: success definitions & exit scenarios for CuraHealth eval

Hi Susan — attached is MAP_v1.1 with the clinical/non-clinical split and the procurement staging clause called out on the final sheet. Key asks before we lock timeline: 

1) Procurement: confirm PO + 30d provisional staging is acceptable (Procurement team asked for a short SOW paragraph; see attachment).
2) Security: confirm the list of audit artifacts you want for the sample (admin logs, access logs, KMS access traces).
3) Demo attendees: confirm Dr. Patel and Lindsay will attend the stakeholder demo (we'll schedule 60 minutes).

If we get confirmations by Thursday EOD, proposed timeline becomes:
- Week A (next week): Redwood test harness + golden set run
- Week B: performance/stress run + security artifact collection
- Week C: stakeholder demo + signoff / PO-staged handoff

Attachment: MAP_v1.1_CuraHealth.xlsx; acceptance-smoke-scripts.md

Thanks — Ben

Ben / Team — we reviewed the updated MAP_v1.1 and it looks good. Confirming: 

- Procurement: PO + 30d provisional staging is approved (Procurement will issue PO by Monday).
- Security: we'll accept the sample artifacts you listed (admin logs, access logs).
- Demo: Dr. Patel and Lindsay available for a demo on Week C; please send two time options.

Please proceed with the test harness run next week. Once we have the PO we'll finalize the SOW language, but this is sufficient to start the pilot activity.

— Susan
